Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First i contacted my own university to know if they had an exchange arrangement already. There after i called Bergen university, that explanied me when og who i should contact at the same time as getting my pre-approval of the courses from KU.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Study counceling both on phone and e-mail. And when i came also a contact person I could meet with.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the clinical rotation i wanted, so very succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be in good time

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Clinical rotation at a hospital.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was a clinical rotation of my first half of my 6th year og medical education. Therefor the courses had to match the clinical skills one should could learn at a hospital similar to the one in my study programe.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similiar in that way I was at a clinical rotation, so I followed docters around the hospital and they tought my clinical skills. There were alot of lectures in the week, that the staff attended to. This is also very similiar, when I have been in a clinical rotation from UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Clinical rotation - "emergency department" and "neurology" as a part of my fifth perspective. "Internationale perspektiver - med klinik i udlandet":

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely a clinical rotation in a another country, if this is possible.

questions.answer: There was BSI Friluft, which was an outdoor organisation, so they arranged hiking trips, skiing trips, climbing etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Outdoor activities! Best way to meet new people and appreciate the nature.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on a trip a bit away from the study city, just to get some more perspective. Or go on your in the city and explore museeums, local hangout places.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was also in scandinavia. Norway vs denmark have many similarities. So in this case it was okay easy, but ofcourse the language is different, which made it more difficult in the beginning.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Yes, learn the language.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: language.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Nature hangout and the slow life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't be shy to talk to strangers, seek out oppurtonities that are outisde the faculty.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to learn a bit of the language.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Nature experience, and meeting new people on my own.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To be alone without friends and family.
